O*NET 29-1243.00 describes surgical evaluation, surgery, and postoperative follow-up for fetuses, newborns, children, and adolescents; any real surgery and medical decision is carried out by a qualified team with institutional authorization.

Use two fully fictional pediatric patient records for a non-clinical paper exercise: verify whether the preoperative material is complete, whether versions are consistent, and whether guardian consent and anesthesia assessment are documented, and write the doubts and the handoff recipients. Signals for continuing to explore: willingness to undertake long medical training, verify evidence, explain clearly to families, and pause the process and escalate to an authorized physician when information is insufficient. Caution applies if someone wants to bypass mentoring, ignore record contradictions, or decide surgery from tool output alone.

This card uses the O*NET 29-1243.00 tasks, the exact US BLS occupational row, and physician qualification material for editorial judgment; it is not an individual ability assessment, surgical training, or Chinese practice license statement. If you are interested in pediatric surgical evaluation, team collaboration, and high-responsibility clinical work, first learn about physician training, registration, specialty training, and institutional authorization in the target region; then use fictional material verification exercises to observe whether you can identify information gaps and hand off clearly.

Pediatric surgeons evaluate surgical diseases and injuries in fetuses, newborns, children, and adolescents, judge intervention needs from history, examination, and specialty consultation, explain perioperative matters to guardians, perform surgery within qualifications and institutional authorization, and follow up. Real medical decisions are not made by web pages or tools.

O*NET 29-1243.00 lists pediatric examination, judging surgical necessity, family communication, surgical team coordination, and postoperative recovery monitoring; the exact BLS 29-1243 row separately provides 2025 pay, employment, and the 2025—2035 projection. Task descriptions and the statistical period cannot be conflated.
